title: Solar Panels for Commercial and Residential Buildings
what_it_is: Solar Panels for Commercial and Residential Buildings

sections.label: Solar panel deployment approach
sections.summary: Singapore takes a practical approach to scaling up solar panels, aiming for 350 MWp by 2020 on 5,000 HDB blocks and 100 Government buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Second, the cost-effectiveness of solar panels depends on the location of the building, and the exposure of the rooftop to direct sunlight.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Hence, instead of a mandatory requirement for all buildings, we take a practical approach in scaling up the deployment of solar panels on such building rooftops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: With demand aggregation, we plan to increase solar generation capacity to 350-megawatt peak (MWp) by 2020, with solar panels deployed on around 5,000 Housing and Development Board blocks and 100 Government buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: In addition, the Building and Construction Authority Green Mark Scheme encourages the adoption of renewable energy sources, which include solar power.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To date, about 20 MWp of solar panels are due to be installed in our Green Mark projects.

sections.label: No mandatory solar panel mandate
sections.summary: Mandating solar panels across all buildings is not commercially sensible due to limited rooftop space, shading, and low potential to meet total electrical demand.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Indeed, we are always watching what other people are doing and trying to adopt best practices and also to see how the technology evolves as far as solar photovoltaic panels are concerned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But, today, because of the competing uses on limited rooftop space, and the bigger challenge being the fact that rooftops can be shaded by a building nearby, I think, commercially, it would not make sense for us to mandate that across all buildings, because then you would have installed the solar panels and not get any use out of them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Hypothetically, even if we were to install panels across all our rooftops, that would probably only satisfy about 10% of our total electrical demands.
